binders: Implicit real parameters K (bulkModulus) and rho (density).
A system carrying real-valued pressure p(x,t) and velocity u(x,t) fields and the pointwise system equations encoded by its type.
In the second conjunct, an arbitrary profile f: Real -> Real and arbitrary x,t: Real.
hypotheses: By the system structure, rho != 0 and at every (x,t) the fields have partial derivatives satisfying p_t+K*u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)*p_x=0.
conclusions: With c=sqrt(K/rho) and w=p-rho*c*u, for every x,t there exist the temporal and spatial derivatives w_t and w_x at (x,t), and w_t-c*w_x=0.
For every profile f and every x,t, the traveling-wave expression f(x-(-c)t) equals f(x+c*t).
mathematical_definitions: c is the principal nonnegative real square root sqrt(K/rho).
The pointwise predicate q_t+s*q_x=0 includes existence of both indicated one-variable derivatives at the point.
A traveling wave with profile f and speed s is defined as f(x-s*t).
The system type packages p,u and pointwise differentiability witnesses satisfying the two first-order equations.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive real K and rho and every packaged solution (p,u) of p_t+K u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)p_x=0, let c=sqrt(K/rho). The left-mode variable w=p-rho*c*u satisfies the transport equation w_t-c w_x=0 at every point. In addition, for every profile f, the definition of a traveling wave at speed -c reduces pointwise to f(x+c t).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is restricted to strictly positive real K and rho; the system structure separately carries rho != 0.
All PDE statements are pointwise and encode partial derivatives via one-variable HasDerivAt predicates with the other coordinate fixed.

The theorem quantifies over an already-packaged system, so if no such system exists for given parameters the universal implication is vacuous; constant zero fields nevertheless provide an evident compatible example when rho != 0.
The first conclusion says only that w satisfies a transport equation; it does not assert that every such w has a global profile representation.
The second conjunct is a definitional identity for arbitrary profiles and does not assert that the system's w equals any particular profile f(x+c t).
No initial or boundary conditions, regularity beyond the displayed pointwise first derivatives, uniqueness, or domain other than all real x,t are encoded.
